source: This utterance is a promise if and only if it creates a commitment. This utterance does not create a commitment. Consequently it is not a promise.

reconstruction.title: Argument that the utterance is not a promise

claims.text: This utterance is a promise if and only if it creates a commitment.

evidence.quote: This utterance is a promise if and only if it creates a commitment.

claims.interpretation_note: Biconditional definition of a promise in terms of commitment creation

claims.text: This utterance does not create a commitment.

evidence.quote: This utterance does not create a commitment.

claims.interpretation_note: Negation of the necessary condition for a promise

claims.text: Consequently it is not a promise.

evidence.quote: Consequently it is not a promise.

translations.reason: Logical consequence derived from premises using modus tollens

interpretation_notes: Biconditional (iff) is treated as material equivalence in classical propositional logic
Negation is explicitly encoded as (not Q) rather than lexical negation in predicate meaning
Conclusion follows via modus tollens: from (iff P Q) and (not Q) entails (not P)
